comments.text: Singapore looks clean, rich, safe, and almost perfect. But behind that order is a deeper story about pressure, control, and the real price of perfection. Would you live in a place like this? Comment below. 👇 #Singapore #SingaporeTravel #TravelDocumentary #SingaporeLife #AsiaTravel

comments.author: @rlp_scanner
comments.text:
I applaud the Creator of this Video for portraying Singapore realistically, warts and all.
The images captured are of Singapore’s streets and places, not AI generated nor of some other parts of the world.
Immigrating from Malaysia as a child, I have grown to appreciate this place I call home. Unsentimentally. Yes, I have been fined for Jaywalking once in my youth; copped speeding offenses whilst driving too fast, and I truly abhor the constant humidity & tropical heat inherent in living here.
I would not argue for less enforcement. In fact, it would be good if smoking could be banned here. Don’t flame me, it’s just my personal opinion.
Other than that, IF you are a law abiding and morally upright person, you will never feel restricted/constrained or persecuted as the presence of physical law enforcement is surprisingly low key, street & traffic cameras notwithstanding.
Most importantly, Here We have a Choice. The Majority of Singaporeans have chosen to live with this often ( Western ) derided system of social democracy. We are free ( and working towards or have the means ) to leave at any time we no longer feel at home here.

comments.author: @deedeedee1608
comments.text: I was born here, lived here all my life, over 5 decades, recognise all the blessings of being Singaporean, but no, I would not choose to live here. I am working towards living half the year here and half the year overseas. It's the only way I can continue. With age, I have lost the tolerance to live in this pressure cooker 24/7/365.
